title: Why You Forget Names But Remember Faces
hook: Forgetting a name but recognising a face is a real brain quirk.

narration.text: Forgetting a name but recognising a face is a real brain quirk.
Your brain stores faces as complex visual patterns.
This visual information is processed differently from names.
Names are often arbitrary labels, not linked to a person's appearance.
Faces offer many more cues for retrieval, like hair, eyes, and expressions.
This is why you can recall meeting someone, but not their specific name.
It is not a memory failure, just how your brain organises information.
Does this happen to you often when meeting new people?

description: Ever found yourself knowing a face instantly, but the name just won't come to mind? This video explains the fascinating reason behind this common brain phenomenon. It is all about how your brain processes visual information versus arbitrary linguistic labels.
topic: Why you sometimes struggle to put a name to a familiar face.
